Indicator 1b measures the proportion of newly diagnosed children and young people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who receive all three recommended initial examinations: gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and an MRI scan or capsule endoscopy [^src1]. This metric, tracked by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]], is crucial for ensuring comprehensive and standardized diagnostic workups for pediatric IBD patients across Denmark [^src1].

Nationally, 69% (142 out of 207) of eligible patients received the full recommended diagnostic package [^src1]. Performance varies significantly across the five Danish regions. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and Region Midtjylland lead the regional rankings, achieving 78% (25/32) and 77% (37/48) compliance, respectively [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] trails significantly, with only 38% (8/21) of patients receiving all three examinations [^src1]. The data reveals that this regional shortfall is entirely driven by AAUH Aalborg Børne- og Ungeafdeling, which accounts for all 21 cases in the region and matches the regional average of 38% [^src1].

At the departmental level, several hospitals achieve perfect compliance, acting as leaders in this metric. Herlev Børn og Unge, Rigshospitalet Pædiatrisk Klinik (GGK), and HE Midt Viborg Børn og Unge all report 100% completion rates, though the latter is the most statistically robust among them with 11 out of 11 patients fully examined [^src1]. Other high-performing departments include SUH Roskilde Pædiatri at 90% (19/21) and SLB Kolding Børne- og Ungeafdeling at 87% (20/23) [^src1]. Conversely, NSR Slagelse Pædiatri is a notable outlier at the bottom, completing the full workup for only 33% of its patients, while OUH Odense Børne- og Ungeafdeling H sits at 52% (11/21) [^src1]. Large departments such as [[hvidovre|Hvidovre]] Børne- og Ungeafdeling (67%, 28/42) and [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] (Aarhus Børn og Unge, 68%, 21/31) perform close to the national average, while [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] (Gødstrup Børn og Unge) performs well above it at 83% (5/6) [^src1].

Because the provided data consists of only a single dated section from the 2024 report, no longitudinal trends can be established regarding whether national or regional compliance is improving or declining over time [^src1]. Furthermore, the source document does not specify a formal target threshold (such as a 90% or 95% goal) for this indicator, meaning compliance is evaluated purely on relative performance rather than met or missed standardized targets [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen viser andelen af nydiagnosticerede børn og unge med IBD, der har fået foretaget alle tre anbefalede undersøgelser (gastroskopi, koloskopi og MR-scanning/kapselendoskopi), med stor variation fra 38 % i Region Nordjylland til 100 % på nogle afdelinger, og en national andel på 69 %.
